messages.content: Write a realistic SMS conversation between a patient in rural North Dakota and Northline Care's check-in agent. Patient has hypertension, is frustrated after 30 hours waiting for nurse callback. Patient ID: pt-1005. Conversation #28.

**TEXT 1 (Patient):** "hi pt-1005 here. called about my BP yesterday. when is a nurse gonna call me back? been 30 hours now and getting worried"

**TEXT 2 (Agent):** "Hi there - I can see your concern. Let me check on your nurse callback status right now."

**TEXT 3 (Agent):** "The median response time is currently 31 hours. I know that's frustrating when you're already at 30. A nurse will reach out as soon as possible."

**TEXT 4 (Patient):** "31 HOURS?? So basically another full day after I've already waited all day?? My BP's been high all week! This is ridiculous"

**TEXT 5 (Agent):** "I hear your frustration - that wait isn't ideal, especially in rural areas where you can't just walk in. I can't speed up the nurse callback, but I can make sure they have everything when they call. What's been happening with your BP?"

**TEXT 6 (Patient):** "170s all week. taking my meds. 168/104 this morning, 171/99 yesterday. just freaked it means something bad"

**TEXT 7 (Agent):** "Got those readings logged. I can't advise if something's wrong - that's for the nurse to tell you. But they'll see all this context. Also: if you feel chest pain, shortness of breath, or severe headache before the nurse calls, don't wait - that's 911."

**TEXT 8 (Patient):** "ok. just wish i didnt have to wait another day. thanks anyway"

theme: asks how long a nurse will take to call back, frustrated after 30 hours
